subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: Help me understand what's worth analyzing in these incident tickets.

judge.implied_focus: Incident resolution performance / SLA adherence (how long incidents take to resolve and whether they meet SLA targets)

per_column.name: resolution_hours
per_column.rationale: Directly quantifies time-to-resolution, the core metric of resolution performance and the natural driver of SLA outcomes.

per_column.name: sla_status
per_column.rationale: Binary/categorical outcome of the resolution-performance focus; the target facet an analyst would investigate (407 breached is a strong signal).

per_column.name: priority_tier
per_column.rationale: A key predictor/segmentation attribute for resolution time and SLA breach, letting an analyst slice performance by urgency.

per_column.name: topic_cluster
per_column.rationale: Groups incidents by problem domain, a coherent explanatory dimension for why certain categories breach SLA or take longer.

judge.rationale: The four columns cohere tightly around a single inferable focus: resolution performance and SLA adherence. resolution_hours (metric) and sla_status (outcome) form the core, while priority_tier and topic_cluster provide coherent predictor/segmentation facets to explain variation in that outcome. This is a genuine analytical structure (outcome + drivers) at a useful granularity, not a restatement or mechanical grab-bag. Minor deductions: resolution_hours and sla_status are partly redundant derivations of the same underlying timing, and no facet touches ownership/team (assignment_group) which would strengthen the causal structure; but the set is clearly focused and actionable (heavy breach rate is an obvious investigable signal).
